title: Intraoperative VIM thalamus microelectrode recordings during transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS) for essential tremor (Luu et al.; derivative: authors' processed 48 kHz signals)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the ventral intermediate (VIM) thalamus region of 9 adults with medication-refractory essential tremor undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. At each recording depth, 60 s were recorded with and without transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS), a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation therapy. This derivative repackages the authors' processed, software-filtered 48 kHz signals into BIDS (BrainVision float32), with motion-artifact blanking masks provided as events.
methods_description: Recordings were made with FHC Guideline 4000 LP+ using anterior, center and posterior Ben-gun microelectrodes, each recorded bipolar against a macro contact. Sampling was at 48 kHz, with 60 s trials per condition (TAPS off/on) at each depth. The authors' processing applied software low-pass filtering, offset removal and trimming to 60 s, and computed motion-artifact blanking masks.
